answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making each identity prove work before it earns any say. A newcomer stakes collateral, accepts randomized jobs, and gathers attestations from reviewers outside its cluster. A cipher binds every result to its signer, a dune of accumulated history buries forged accounts, and a sparrow's small reward cap prevents cheap farming at scale. Audits slash faked bonds, so duplicating identities adds cost and scrutiny rather than influence.
